detailedSolution: Maltose is composed of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units joined by an $\alpha-1,4$-glycosidic linkage. The $C_1$ of the first glucose is bonded to $C_4$ of the second glucose. The hemiacetal group at $C_1$ of the second glucose residue is free, allowing ring opening in solution to yield a free aldehyde group capable of reducing Tollens' and Fehling's solutions.
